question.text: By what time must mutual fund schemes (other than liquid and overnight funds) disclose their NAV on every business day?

answer.text: By 11:00 PM on the same business day
By 9:00 AM on the next business day
By 3:00 PM on the same business day
By 8:00 AM on the same business day

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI's NAV-disclosure framework for mutual funds, schemes other than liquid and overnight funds are required to compute and publish their NAV at the end of every business day. SEBI circulars on NAV upload specify an evening deadline (11:00 PM on the same business day) for non-liquid schemes, with liquid and overnight funds following a separate next-day timeline. The intent is to ensure all unitholders see a fresh, comparable NAV for that business day before the next trading day begins. The Trap: 9:00 AM next day pushes disclosure outside the same-day window. 3:00 PM is the application cut-off for transactions, not the NAV upload deadline. 8:00 AM same day is too early — NAV can only be computed after close of markets and overnight valuation. The 11:00 PM evening deadline aligns with operational realities of end-of-day valuation and upload. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.106, p.218) state that NAV is disclosed at the end of each business day and uploaded as per applicable guidelines, but the explicit 11:00 PM same-business-day deadline is not stated in the pages checked. The framing above is general SEBI-circular knowledge on NAV disclosure timelines.
